title: Faith perceives its object less clearly, yet assents more firmly
source_text: XL. Itaque fides, qua verbum divinum amplectimur, objectum suum quidem minus clare percipit, quam assensus, qui locum habet in scientiis humanis: verumtamen fidei assensus in mente firmior est, eamque potentius & efficacius afficit, ac altius penetrat: ita ut quemvis alium assensum potius quam hunc fidelis paratus sit excutere.
pass_a_gloss: And so faith, by which we embrace the divine word, perceives its object indeed less clearly than the assent which has place in the human sciences: yet the assent of faith is firmer in the mind, and affects it more powerfully and efficaciously, and penetrates more deeply — so that the faithful is ready to cast off any other assent rather than this.
pass_b_english: Object less clear than in human sciences.
Yet faith-assent firmer, stronger, deeper in the mind.
Ready to shake off any other assent first.
